title: Case 1: Territorial Extent of Laws & Extra-Territorial Nexus (Article 245 • Writ Petition)
legalTheme: Part XI: Relations between the Union and the States • Article 245
factualMatrix: Before the Supreme Court of India (Article 32), an aggrieved petitioner challenged an impugned executive notification and enforcement order issued by the Union Ministry / Central Authority under Article 245 (Territorial Extent of Laws & Extra-Territorial Nexus) of Part XI (Relations between the Union and the States). Relying on the core guarantee that Defines the geographical reach of Union and State laws, empowering Parliament to make laws for all or any part of India and laws with extraterritorial operation, while State legislatures are confined to their respective state territories. and citing State of Bombay v. F.N. Balsara (1951), the petitioner sought judicial invalidation for violating constitutional limits and procedural fairness.
framingQuestions: 1. Whether the Writ Petition before the Supreme Court of India (Article 32) is maintainable under Article 245?
2. Does the Union Ministry / Central Authority's executive notification and enforcement order conform to Article 245 (Territorial Extent of Laws & Extra-Territorial Nexus)?
3. How does State of Bombay v. F.N. Balsara (1951) govern the constitutional validity and relief in this matter?
statutoryApplicability: State of Bombay v. F.N. Balsara (1951)
modelAnswer:
1. MAINTAINABILITY: The Writ Petition before the Supreme Court of India (Article 32) is maintainable as it raises a direct constitutional question under Article 245 (Part XI).

2. SUBSTANTIVE ANALYSIS (Article 245): Defines the geographical reach of Union and State laws, empowering Parliament to make laws for all or any part of India and laws with extraterritorial operation, while State legislatures are confined to their respective state territories. Applying the governing principle—'Territorial competence (Art 245) and subject matter competence governed by the 7th Schedule.'—the impugned executive notification and enforcement order by the Union Ministry / Central Authority must strictly satisfy constitutional bounds.

3. PRECEDENT (State of Bombay v. F.N. Balsara (1951)) & RELIEF: Guided by State of Bombay v. F.N. Balsara (1951), any overreach inconsistent with Article 245 is liable to be quashed or suitably restrained.
